findings.finding: The design must not claim transactional exactly-once behavior across EventGraph, Work, Git, and GitHub.
findings.evidence: The scheduler defines deterministic attempts, reconcile-before-retry, conflict blocking, and effect idempotency while rejecting a distributed-transaction claim.

findings.finding: The v1 service must not inherit or republish tracked credential-looking configuration found during checkpoint audit.
findings.evidence: The topology requires fresh mode-0600 configuration, forbids reading hive/loop/config.env, and requires a secret-safe audit.

findings.finding: The exact independent reviewer named by the packet must be available and able to emit the governed schema.
findings.evidence: After two preserved nonconforming Ollama/Qwen attempts, Claude CLI became authenticated and passed a non-mutating output probe; v1.0.2 binds the eligible Claude/Anthropic family.

residual_risks: GitHub effects are reconciled and idempotent but cannot be transactionally committed with local EventGraph and Work state.
The v1 scheduler is intentionally single-instance; multi-host leader election remains v2.
The demonstration supports one author family and one independent reviewer family.
The installed governance cache has a noncanonical bytecode extra; gate evidence binds exact source files and result artifacts instead of claiming manifest parity.
non_authorizations: No production deployment or CanOperate expansion.
No direct default-branch push, branch-protection change, or merge of demonstration PRs.
No mutation or reuse of Operation #86 or other consumed evidence.
No credential reuse, disclosure, or evidence fabrication.
No value allocation or residual-risk closure.
